Human rights are universally recognized moral principles or norms that establish standards of human behavior and are often protected by both national and international laws . [ 1 ] These rights are considered inherent and inalienable, meaning they belong to every individual simply by virtue of being human , regardless of characteristics like nationality, ethnicity, religion, gender, sexual orientation, disability, caste, or socioeconomic status. They encompass a broad range of civil, political, economic, social, and cultural rights, such as the right to life , freedom of speech , protection against enslavement , and right to education .
